Shrimp Tank Log

Entry 4 - Pearlweed and soil obtained

April 19, 2026

It’s 3:45 pm. I’m in West Lakeview, saying goodbye to my friend and best of luck to his future as I head out from his first big gallery show in...

It’s 3:45 pm. I’m in West Lakeview, saying goodbye to my friend and best of luck to his future as I head out from his first big gallery show in Chicago. Due to Visa issues under the current administration, he’s being forced out of the country by this summer. If anyone reading this has ties to press/journalism and wants to help, his case for reapplication would strongly benefit from more published media.

My pearlweed contact is only a 7 minute drive away. I notice a Menards right by his place, so I make a quick pit stop and successfully pick up some soil!!!! It’s perfect: organic, non-fertilized, in a small enough quantity, and only about 3 bucks. What luck. I misjudge the amount of parking spots open by his place and accidentally park a block further than I need to and make my way to his building, where a small ziplock bag of pearlweed with my name on it is waiting in the foyer. With my large plant pickkup scheduled for the next day, I had asked for just 5 stems, but my pearlweed guy insisted that they were small and wouldn’t give me under 10 for $5, and could do 20 for $7, so I ended up with the latter.

Back home, I’m greeted with a number of packages. I unbox my orders of aquascaping tools, aquarium siphon, water testing strips, aquarium light, tap water conditioner, and gravel substrate.

Things are coming together.

Entry 3 - Scouting day

April 17, 2026

Today is a scouting day. I’m on the hunt for substrate. My first stop is Golden Aquarium in west Bridgeport. Going in, I’m greeted by the sound of trickling water...

Today is a scouting day. I’m on the hunt for substrate. My first stop is Golden Aquarium in west Bridgeport. Going in, I’m greeted by the sound of trickling water and the largest set of fake breasts I have ever seen. The customer appears to be a regular, based on their friendly interaction with the shop owner. I comb through the available gravel and find one good option, but the colors are brighter than I prefer. One of the workers asks what I’m looking for, and I explain my predicament. The boss says there should be some gravel in the boxes by the entrance, and I walk around the store as they unpack their shipment. I study the plants for sale — someone of them are starting to look familiar — and take note of their shrimp and snail stock for the future. No blue shrimp at this location. The worker tells me they don’t have any more gravel in the size I want.

I find black sand next door at the PetCo, but it’s too fine. The Ace hardware in the same strip only had large bags of soil and their buckets were unattractive. Back in my car, I put a 10lb bag of 2-4 mm aquarium gravel in “midnight pearl” in my Amazon cart. It’s really more of a brick colour overall, but I’m happy with it.

Just because, I drive another 12 minutes to Home Depot, and the situation is dire. The soil options are either too big in quantity or the same as Target, except that they seem to come with a gnat problem. The buckets are nicer, but the intense orange would make it difficult to see clearly if I needed to. They didn’t have the lamp screw I was looking for outside of this project either.

I end up getting a white bucket from the Ace hardware on in Hyde Park on my way back.

More money to Amazon.

Entry 2 - Plant dealing

April 16, 2026

On the way back from class, I visit Target to check out my local soil options. Organic and non fertilized is what I’m looking for, and I do find one...

On the way back from class, I visit Target to check out my local soil options. Organic and non fertilized is what I’m looking for, and I do find one that seems like it should work. Though a bit more expensive than I would have liked, it was good to know I had something nearby to fall back on.

I’ve looked at pretty much every aquatic plant listing in the Chicago area on FB marketplace at this point and my options are rather meager. ~It doesn’t make much sense for me to be running all over town for a few trimmings here and there, especially when I (don’t know what plants I want/need/are available).~

I find a somewhat recent posting on the r/ChicagoAquaSwap community on Reddit. It’s crossposted from the larger r/Aquaswap subreddit and features a list of latin names that I don’t recognize, but the title says “easy beginner plant bundle” and the price seems reasonable. Everything from the post is already marked as sold, so I leave a comment asking if they have any stock available for this weekend.

They get back to me within 10 minutes with a list of available plants. After some googling, I let them know I’m interested in everything aside from the creeping Jenny (for reasons unknown. Genuinely don’t remember why). We make plans to pickup the following Monday evening.

I finally pull the trigger on an order of siphon tube pump, cheap water testing strips, some long tweezers and curved scissors, and water conditioner off Amazon.

Entry 1 - Tank obtained

April 15, 2026

It’s 2:30pm and I’m driving up to Logan square for a rimless 5G tank. These things typically run for around $60, so I was very pleased with $35 I got...

It’s 2:30pm and I’m driving up to Logan square for a rimless 5G tank. These things typically run for around $60, so I was very pleased with $35 I got it for. Snagging a parking spot by construction scaffolding of Ramen Wasabi, I wait for my contact to arrive. A black sedan pulls by a few minutes later, and the beautiful butch explains she had too many tanks already and apologizes for the cat hair, though I didn’t see any in the tank. She asks if I had been to the restaurant before and says it’s her favourite place in the city. “I’m going to walk in and pretend I’m in not coming in half an hour before closing” she says as a goodbye.

I begin speaking to local aquatic plant sellers. I find someone in Lakeview, an uchicago alumni according to his profile, selling Pearlweed (a desired plant!). Though I can’t tell if he’s just saying it to be nice, I earnestly ask his recommendations for equipment and suppliers and he kindly humors me. We make plans to pick up on Sunday.

Inception. With a push from Professor Buse and roughly 5 weeks left in the quarter, I should have enough time for fauna.

I spend my evening making a general list of equipment I wanted/needed and scrolling Facebook Marketplace for supplies. If I want to get this tank cycled and fully set up before the end of the quarter, I’m going to have to move fast and local.
